figures.caption: Predicted time of the first bearing failure, issued at four times as data arrives: the particle filter's 90% and 50% intervals and median, with open-loop's 90% interval faint below, against the true failure time. An open arrow marks an interval reaching past the forecast horizon: every particle-filter 90% interval here extends past it, so its coverage partly reflects wide upper tails (calibrated but not sharp). As data arrives, the particle filter's lower bound rises from ~16k to ~24k h and its median moves toward the true failure time. The unit is chosen by rule: the median particle-filter |log(median RUL / true RUL)| among units still running at the last issue (6 of 20; this favours longer-lived units). All units are in F11.

The pipeline on the Eversys coffee machine, from its manual (PDF) to a twin and forecasts: each box is a phase with this lineage's counts, read from its artifacts, and the phase's cold-run API cost (all cached calls batched to none batched). Estimate and evaluate run on synthetic data generated from the twin.

Cold-run API cost per phase, the new pipeline against the legacy prototype (M1 baseline, its steps mapped onto the new phases). The new bar spans every cached LLM call batched (dark) to none batched (light). Phases at $0 in both are left out. From each machine's evaluation report.

Where each parameter comes from (left), and which sources carry the remaining-life uncertainty (right: share of var(log RUL) at t = 0 under the priors). Eversys has no manual parameter: its calibrated lives rest on cleaning intervals declared in machine.toml. Judged lives dominate the uncertainty on every machine.

Calibrated but not sharp. Left: posterior over prior 90% width of each part's life, median over units at the last issue; the data narrows only the parts an observation reaches. Right: median 90% interval width over the true RUL per observed quantity; an arrow means more than half of those intervals reach past the horizon.

Health with and without the documented maintenance, simulated on each machine's verified twin: at the prior medians (lines) and over 60 prior draws (5-95% bands). The milk system's daily cleaning is declared in machine.toml (deployment); the air filter's cleaning and replacement intervals come from the manual.
notes: derived by simulation: 60 prior draws per profile (synthesize's draw_unit, seed 20261118) and one run at the prior medians, on the lineage's verified twin and ParamSet

figures.caption: What if the water filter is replaced late (1.5x its W-014 point)? Left: each boiler's time to its scaling limit on a new machine. notes: What-if on the twin's own assumptions: W-014 does not identify a boiler's k or the coupling strength r (their posteriors are their priors), so the change shown comes from the coupling form, r's default prior and the boilers' judged lives; it is not validated against failure data.
